name: China

covers.summary: For a front bumper (M1) the regulatory map establishes no bumper-specific certification route in China. The assembly is assessed through vehicle-level standards – low-speed protection (GB 17354 family; replacement designation and transition unresolved) and pedestrian protection (GB 24550-2024, implementation 1 Jan 2025) – and through function-specific standards for what is integrated in it: lighting (GB 5920-2024, GB 4599-2024, installation GB 4785-2019), the licence-plate bracket (GB 15741-1995), the towing device (GB 32087) and the LiDAR (GB 44703-2024). Radio, EMC, driver-assistance and EV charge-port requirements are still open. All of this is a screening reference from a research draft that was not independently reverified, not a compliance result.

certification.scheme: Not established for the bumper assembly
certification.type: vehicle-level assessment; no component-level route established in the regulatory map
certification.summary: The regulatory map names no compulsory-certification or self-declaration route for a front-bumper assembly in China (the CCC rule found for rear lamps does not cover it). Integrated lamps are certified as lighting devices; the rest is assessed at vehicle level.

summary: China is not a party to the UNECE 1958 Agreement and does not recognise E approvals; rear lamps need mandatory CCC certification under CNCA-C11-07:2026 (type testing in a designated Chinese lab, factory inspection, ongoing surveillance) and a CCC mark on the product. Since 1 Jul 2025 the technical basis is the consolidated standards GB 5920-2024 (light-signalling devices, incl. tail, stop and reversing lamps) and GB 11564-2024 (retro-reflectors); installation on the vehicle follows GB 4785-2019. For stop and reversing lamps, GB 5920-2024 applies to new types from the 19th month after it took effect, and to existing approvals from the 37th month.

standards.title: 汽车和挂车光信号装置及系统 / Light-signalling devices and systems for motor vehicles and their trailers
standards.scope: Mandatory standard (强标), published 29 Sep 2024, in force since 1 Jul 2025. Covers light-signalling devices on vehicles of categories M, N and O, including front/rear position lamps (tail lamps), stop lamps, reversing lamps, direction indicators, rear fog lamps, licence plate lamps, side marker lamps and light-signal projection units. According to a secondary source it replaces GB 5920-2019, GB 15235-2007, GB 11554-2008, GB 17509-2008, GB 18408-2015, GB 18409-2013, GB 18099-2013 and GB 23255-2019, among others. Colour requirements refer to GB 4785.

standards.title: 机动车回复反射装置 / Retro-reflective devices and markings for motor vehicles
standards.scope: Mandatory standard, published 29 Sep 2024, in force since 1 Jul 2025. Retro-reflectors and rear marking plates for motor vehicles. According to a secondary source it replaces GB 11564-2008, GB 19151-2003, GB 23254-2009 and GB 25990-2010.

standards.title: 汽车及挂车外部照明和光信号装置的安装规定 / Prescription for installation of the external lighting and light-signalling devices for motor vehicles and their trailers
standards.scope: Mandatory installation rule (vehicle level), published 17 Dec 2019, in force since 1 Jul 2020, replaces GB 4785-2007; still valid according to the SAMR portal (as of 2026-10-25). Sets the number, layout, alignment, wiring and colour of the lamps, including tail lamps, reversing lamps and retro-reflectors.

standards.title: 汽车及挂车前位灯、后位灯、示廓灯和制动灯配光性能 / Photometric characteristics of front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps and stop lamps
standards.scope: Previous standard for position and stop lamps (in force from 1 Jan 2020); withdrawn according to the SAMR portal (废止), replaced by GB 5920-2024. Only still relevant for existing approvals within the transition periods of GB 5920-2024.

standards.title: 汽车及挂车倒车灯配光性能 / Photometric characteristics of reversing lamps for power-driven vehicles
standards.scope: Previous standard for reversing lamps (in force from 1 Jun 2008); withdrawn according to the SAMR portal (废止), content moved into GB 5920-2024.

standards.title: Front and rear protective devices for passenger cars (low-speed protection)
standards.scope: Bumper standard. An official project record identifies a replacement, but the final designation, effective edition and transition are unresolved (verification required, GAP-001).

standards.title: Protection of motor vehicle for pedestrians in the event of a collision
standards.scope: Mandatory national standard, implementation 1 Jan 2025. Whole-vehicle performance to which fascia, absorber and lower stiffener contribute; M1/N1 scope is subject to exclusions and transition clauses. Pedestrian-impact sensors are in scope where they are part of the vehicle's pedestrian-protection system.

standards.title: Protection of occupants in frontal collision
standards.scope: Whole-vehicle reference for the crash-energy-management structure, not a standalone approval of fascia or absorber. The current edition requires confirmation: the source cited is related official context, not direct verification of this edition (GAP-020).

standards.title: Licence plates/brackets and their position on motor vehicles and trailers
standards.scope: Mandatory national standard. Applies to the front licence-plate bracket and position.

standards.title: Light vehicle towing devices
standards.scope: Screening reference only: designation, current edition and cover-related implications are not established (verification required, GAP-021). The source is a policy listing, not the standard text.

standards.title: Road illumination devices and systems for motor vehicles
standards.scope: Mandatory national standard with a function-specific transition (certificates of previously certified products to be converted by 1 Jul 2028 according to the CQC notice). Applies to front fog or other road-illumination lamps integrated in the bumper.

standards.title: General requirements for optical radiation safety
standards.scope: Mandatory national standard, implementation 1 Oct 2026. Scope screening needed for an integrated LiDAR.

standards.title: Safety of laser products – Part 1: Equipment classification and requirements
standards.scope: Recommended national standard (not mandatory by itself), implementation 1 Apr 2025. Assessment reference for laser classification and safety of a LiDAR.

standards.title: Requirements for prohibited substances on automobiles
standards.scope: Recommended national standard; mandatory status is not inferred. Screens vehicles and parts for lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBBs and PBDEs, with limits and exemptions. Applies as a screening reference to rear lamps and front bumpers.

certification.scheme: CCC (China Compulsory Certification), implementation rule CNCA-C11-07:2026 "机动车外部照明及光信号装置（试行）"
certification.type: third-party type approval (type testing + initial factory inspection + surveillance after the certificate is issued)
certification.marking: CCC mark, printed or moulded by the applicant on the outer surface of the product or on the type plate in a clearly visible place; must be permanent and recognisable without damaging the vehicle/product
certification.summary: With announcement 2026 No. 4 (dated 11 Apr 2026), the CNCA issued rule CNCA-C11-07:2026 for exterior lamps and light-signalling devices on vehicles of categories M, N, O and L, valid from 1 Jul 2026. Test standards include GB 5920 and GB 11564 (generally the latest version). Process: application to a designated certification body with a product description and a list of key parts, type testing in a designated lab chosen by the applicant (usually 30 days at most), initial factory inspection including a conformity control plan, then surveillance (follow-up inspections, spot checks at the factory, port or market). Certificates are valid for 5 years; changes to key parts, raw materials or test standards require a certificate change before delivery. Individual components (lenses, reflectors, bulbs) and separately moulded stand-alone retro-reflectors are outside the scope.

deviations.topic: Mandatory CCC certification instead of E approval
deviations.national_requirement: Exterior lamps and light-signalling devices for vehicles of categories M, N, O and L are subject to Chinese compulsory certification under CNCA-C11-07:2026 (valid from 1 Jul 2026). Certification model: type testing in a designated lab + initial factory inspection (quality assurance capability and product conformity) + surveillance after the certificate is issued. Testing covers all applicable points of the test standard (GB 5920, GB 11564). For light-signalling devices, 2 sample lamps including light sources must be submitted. An E approval under UN R148 does not replace the CCC; China is not a party to the 1958 Agreement and the rule does not provide for recognising foreign approvals.
deviations.suggestion: Apply for CCC certification with a designated certification body, plan type testing to GB 5920-2024 in a designated Chinese lab with 2 sealed production samples (incl. light sources and control unit, if any), and add the CCC process (testing, factory audit, certificate) to the project plan as a milestone before the China start of production.

deviations.national_requirement: The applicant must print or mould the CCC mark in a clearly visible place on the outer surface of the product or on the type plate. It must be permanent and stay recognisable when installed, without damaging the vehicle or the product (CNCA-C11-07:2026, section 18). The E approval mark required by UN R148 does not meet this obligation.
deviations.suggestion: Add the CCC mark, moulded into the housing or lens tool or as a permanent print in a place that is visible when installed, and add its position, size and design to the marking drawing in the specification.

deviations.topic: Integrated retro-reflector: separate test standard GB 11564-2024
deviations.national_requirement: Retro-reflectors fall under GB 11564-2024 (in force since 1 Jul 2025). Under CNCA-C11-07:2026, certification units are formed separately per test standard (GB 5920 for light-signalling devices, GB 11564 for retro-reflective devices). For combination lamps with an integrated retro-reflector, 10 additional retro-reflector samples must be submitted. The test report covers, among other things, the coefficient of luminous intensity (CIL), colour, temperature resistance, water and dust tightness, resistance to fuel and lubricating oil, impact strength and corrosion. Type, class, shape, dimensions, material and colour of the retro-reflector must be stated in the product description. Separately moulded stand-alone retro-reflectors are outside the scope of the rule.
deviations.suggestion: Have the integrated retro-reflector additionally tested to GB 11564-2024 as part of the CCC application, provide 10 production samples of the retro-reflector, and document its class, shape, dimensions, material and colour in the specification.

deviations.topic: Test standard GB 5920-2024 and transition periods
deviations.national_requirement: GB 5920-2024 (in force since 1 Jul 2025) replaces, among others, GB 5920-2019 (position and stop lamps) and GB 15235-2007 (reversing lamps); according to the SAMR standards portal both old standards are withdrawn. Under section 11 of the standard, it applies to new types of position lamps from the date it took effect, to new types of stop and reversing lamps from the 19th month (i.e. from 1 Jan 2027) and to already type-approved devices from the 37th month (i.e. from 1 Jul 2028). When a standard changes, the CCC certificate must be switched over within the deadline set by the authority (CNCA-C11-07:2026, 17.2.1).
deviations.suggestion: Order type testing directly to GB 5920-2024 (no longer to GB 5920-2019 or GB 15235-2007), and plan the switch of existing CCC certificates to GB 5920-2024 by July 2028 at the latest.

deviations.topic: Documentation of materials and key parts (outer lens)
deviations.national_requirement: The CCC application requires a product description covering, among other things, the material and coating of the outer lens, light colour, light source type or LED modules, reflector material, and a list of key parts and raw materials with name, type, specification and supplier (CNCA-C11-07:2026, annex 3). The test samples must match production in key parts and raw materials. Technical changes to safety-relevant key parts or raw materials require an approved certificate change; without it the products may not be delivered, sold or imported (17.2.1). The certification body decides which parts count as key parts (13.3).
deviations.suggestion: Fix the PMMA type (manufacturer, trade name, colour), coating and supplier of the red outer lens, plus all other key parts (LED modules, reflector, retro-reflector), in the specification, and set up a change process that reports every change of material or supplier to the CCC certification body before it is made.

deviations.topic: Factory inspection and conformity control plan
deviations.national_requirement: The initial factory inspection checks quality assurance capability and product conformity. The inspection team has at least 2 people, the lamp must be in production during the inspection, and top management must attend the opening and closing meetings. The manufacturer must draw up a conformity control plan (一致性控制计划) and submit a yearly report on how it is implemented. After certification there are follow-up inspections and/or spot checks at the factory, the port or in the market (CNCA-C11-07:2026, sections 7, 12, 14 and annex 1).
deviations.suggestion: Draw up a CCC conformity control plan for the production plant according to annex 1 of the rule, prepare the factory audit (running production, plant management present), and build the yearly implementation report and spot checks into the quality process.

deviations.topic: Low-speed bumper protection: GB 17354 family, replacement unresolved
deviations.national_requirement: Front and rear protective devices of passenger cars are covered by the GB 17354 family (legacy edition GB 17354-1998, low-speed protection). The official project record names a replacement, but the final designation, effective edition and transition have not been established (regulatory map GAP-001, status verification_required).
deviations.suggestion: Confirm with the certification body or the vehicle maker which GB 17354 edition applies to the vehicle programme and from when, and plan the low-speed impact verification of fascia, absorber and lower stiffener against that edition.

deviations.national_requirement: GB 24550-2024 (protection of motor vehicles for pedestrians in a collision; mandatory, implementation 1 Jan 2025) applies to the whole vehicle, and fascia, absorber and lower stiffener contribute to the result. M1/N1 scope is subject to exclusions and transition clauses. Pedestrian-impact sensors count only where they are part of the vehicle's pedestrian-protection system.
deviations.suggestion: Give the vehicle maker the pedestrian-impact data of fascia, absorber and lower stiffener (energy absorption, stiffness), say whether the pedestrian-impact sensors belong to the pedestrian-protection system, and confirm the exclusions and transition clauses of GB 24550-2024 for the target vehicle.

deviations.topic: Frontal occupant protection: GB 11551 edition unconfirmed
deviations.national_requirement: GB 11551-2014 (protection of occupants in a frontal collision) is a whole-vehicle reference for the crash-energy-management structure, not a standalone approval of fascia or absorber. The current edition has not been confirmed from a direct authoritative text (GAP-020).
deviations.suggestion: Confirm the current GB 11551 edition with the vehicle maker and document the crash-energy-management structure (absorber, lower stiffener) so it can be integrated in the vehicle assessment.

deviations.topic: Front licence-plate bracket and position: GB 15741-1995
deviations.national_requirement: GB 15741-1995 (mandatory) sets requirements for licence plates, their brackets and their position on motor vehicles and trailers; it applies to the front plate holder in the bumper.
deviations.suggestion: Check the front plate holder (bracket and position) against GB 15741-1995 together with the vehicle maker.

deviations.national_requirement: GB 32087 (light vehicle towing devices) is only a screening reference: designation, current edition and cover-related implications are not confirmed (GAP-021). The actual accessibility and operation of the towing device behind the cover must be checked.
deviations.suggestion: Verify the designation and edition of GB 32087 and check that the towing-device cover does not impede access to or use of the towing device.

deviations.topic: Integrated lighting: classification by function (GB 5920-2024, GB 4599-2024, GB 4785-2019)
deviations.national_requirement: Lamps integrated in the bumper are classified by their actual function. Signalling functions (daytime running or position lamp, side signalling) fall under GB 5920-2024 with its function-specific transition, front fog or other road-illumination lamps under GB 4599-2024, and installation under GB 4785-2019. The luminous-logo provisions of GB 5920-2024 are not a blanket permission for decorative lighting. The plastic lens is assessed as part of the finished lighting device, not by its resin designation (PC, PMMA) alone.
deviations.suggestion: Classify each integrated lamp by function (signalling, road illumination, decorative), assign it to GB 5920-2024 or GB 4599-2024, check its installation against GB 4785-2019, and do not rely on the PC lens grade alone.

deviations.national_requirement: GB 44703-2024 (general requirements for optical radiation safety; mandatory, implementation 1 Oct 2026) needs a scope screening for the integrated LiDAR. GB/T 7247.1-2024 (laser product safety, classification) is the recommended assessment reference, not a standalone mandatory law.
deviations.suggestion: Screen the LiDAR against the scope of GB 44703-2024, classify it under GB/T 7247.1-2024 and ask the sensor supplier for its optical-safety classification report.

deviations.topic: Radio, EMC and driver-assistance functions of the sensors: instruments not identified
deviations.national_requirement: The regulatory map identifies no precise Chinese instrument for the radio authorisation of the radar (operating band and transmitter configuration still to be determined, GAP-004), the keyless-entry aerial (passive antenna, receiver and transmitter to be classified separately, GAP-012), the EMC of the electronic subassemblies (GAP-006) or driver-assistance/AEB functions that use radar or camera (GAP-007, GAP-008). No identified instrument does not mean the function is unregulated.
deviations.suggestion: List operating band and transmitter configuration of the radar and the keyless-entry aerial, and which sensors feed driver-assistance functions, and have the applicable Chinese radio, EMC and driver-assistance requirements identified before the design is frozen.

deviations.topic: EV charge port: Chinese interface and vehicle electrical-safety requirements not verified
deviations.national_requirement: The Chinese inlet, charging-interface and vehicle electrical-safety requirements for the EV charge port are not sufficiently verified (GAP-015). A cosmetic charge-port door or cover is distinct from the inlet, interlock and high-voltage hardware.
deviations.suggestion: Separate the cosmetic charge-port cover from inlet, interlock and high-voltage hardware in the specification and have the Chinese charging-interface and EV electrical-safety requirements identified for the vehicle.

deviations.topic: Exterior projections of fascia and grille: applicable standard not identified
deviations.national_requirement: The standard, edition and clauses that apply to exterior projections of the fascia and grille were not conclusively established (GAP-002).
deviations.suggestion: Identify the applicable standard, edition and clauses for exterior projections of fascia and grille before design freeze.

deviations.national_requirement: GB/T 30512-2014 (requirements for prohibited substances on automobiles) is a recommended national standard: it screens vehicles and parts for lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBBs and PBDEs, including limits and exemptions. Its mandatory status is not inferred, and an OEM specification is not a standalone law.
deviations.suggestion: Collect substance declarations (lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE) from the material suppliers for the bill of materials and check them against the limits and exemptions of GB/T 30512-2014 and the customer's specification.
